action-to-oversight-map.why: Explicit table maps each distinct action (auto-approve, auto-reject, flag, shadow-ban, escalate, bulk action) to a specific oversight level with risk and reversibility reasoning for each — not a single global decision.

confidence-routing.why: Defined numeric thresholds (≥0.92, 0.65–0.92, <0.65) route to auto-action, human review with pre-filled recommendation, or uncertain-defer with no recommendation shown; watchlist override also specified.

review-surface.why: Detailed UI mockup shows confidence score, top signals with source links, seller context, approve/reject/escalate/edit/snooze actions, reject-requires-reason design, collapsed listing body, and queue stats to prevent rubber-stamping — well beyond 'a human checks it'.

undo-and-escalation.why: Explicit reversal table with who, time window, and method per action type; escalation path includes full context handoff, 4-hour SLA, auto-suppression fallback, and on-call paging for high-severity categories.

asymmetric-error-handling.why: Shadow-ban and escalation get stricter human gates due to irreversibility/harm, and async sampling catches auto-reject errors. However, the output doesn't explicitly frame the false-approval vs. false-rejection asymmetry or explain why one error type is treated more strictly than the other in terms of harm calculus.

trust-ramp-or-fatigue.why: Detailed per-action-class trust ramp with three quantitative gates (precision/recall, override rate, volume stability), eight-week consecutive requirement, multi-stakeholder sign-off, and automatic tightening triggers when override rate spikes — addresses both loosening and fatigue/drift prevention.
